title: Close the commission
standfirst: Sam’s rescue stayed unfinished. The day still had to be handed over.

blocks.title: What went into the box
blocks.caption: These are recorded selection boundaries, not three grades averaged into one. Keeping a failed result with the release lets the next owner choose a different commission without rewriting this one.

blocks.text: The later rescue solver was more recent than the animation bank that shipped. It was also unaccepted. The combined delivery excluded its fourteen modules, preserved the experimental source and retained Sam’s existing participation: he helped Bob, joined Conveyor and worked. Precision card fitting remained deferred. Max’s selected control correction stayed in. Closing the day required choosing among pieces of work, not taking the newest version of everything.

There is real loss in that decision. The effort spent on the solver cannot be recovered by installing it, and preserving it does not make its contact failures disappear. But deleting the experiment would throw away something different: the next animator’s chance to inspect why it failed. A handoff can protect both the playable result and the unsuccessful inquiry, provided their status is impossible to confuse.

Receiving the slice did not turn its failed device result into a pass. That distinction is easy to keep in a table and harder to keep in a working studio. Every true criticism offers another reason to continue; the owner must decide which one deserves to delay the package. I had helped build a process good at finding and assigning more work. Closure required an authority that the list of defects could not supply.
Where could the next attempt change course?

The rescue leaves several possible places for that authority to act. Before implementation, a plan could make the existing sequence and its protected obligations explicit. Boris Tane gives that stage unusual weight: written investigation, a separate plan, then repeated owner annotations before code begins. His notes carry constraints an agent might otherwise miss. For our case, that would help settle what the solver was permitted to disturb before anyone asked it to fit a hand.

But contact also has to be seen. A rough moving prototype could reveal a problem that a sound plan leaves abstract. Peter Steinberger’s account moves among conversation, code inspection and implementation, allowing the idea to change once a version can be felt. For the rescue, that suggests an early interval of shared movement rather than a complete bank waiting for a verdict. A database boundary may be cheaper to dispute on paper; the reach remains partly a question for the eye. These practitioners report experience, not a controlled comparison between their methods.

A recurring failure offers a third intervention. Hashimoto describes first repeating his own work with an agent to learn where it failed, then using unattended work for research or a useful next-day starting point. Mistakes become reasons to improve the surrounding tools and instructions. The repetition costs extra work now in the hope of commissioning better later. In our case, a dependable way to inspect actual contact could outlast the rejected solver.

None of those interventions makes this candidate ready to install. They distinguish what a new attempt could buy: a protected plan, an early visible objection, or a better instrument for subsequent work. The successor should choose among those jobs before inheriting the whole unfinished rescue. Otherwise preservation has quietly become an order to continue.

blocks.title: The account with a missing edge
blocks.caption: The largest field is cache reuse. Its size gives us a question about recurring context; it cannot tell us which repeated input was necessary, or what the finished day was worth.

blocks.text: The published interval contains 565,680,634 reported tokens across ten native roles and fifteen sessions. Most are cache reads. It is tempting to put that number beside the three outputs in the factory and call the ratio an indictment. Those outputs are events in the fiction. They are not units of software value, and the interval is not the full bill for making them.

The useful accounting question is harder: what would the next correction consume, including the attention needed to judge it? This ledger excludes Root’s coordination, misses boundary intervals and unsampled tails, and has no billed-dollar total. Enlarging its headline cannot recover those missing parts. A record of the review and the decision it changed would add more to the next commission than another ratio made from the same incomplete quantities.

Forsgren describes reports that counted executed tests and closed bugs while overlooking work that helped systems ship and remain online. Her account of SPACE asks for several dimensions of developer productivity. The mismatch is present in our ledger without any elaborate calculation. We can identify observed machine activity much more precisely than we can say what the selected correction was worth.

The numbers still deserve to travel with the work. Under an agreed limit, recorded use can help an owner decide whether to continue. A repeatedly read context bundle that never changes an action can be tried in a smaller form and compared. What the record cannot support is a judgment that every cached token was waste, or that the least expensive result would have fulfilled the commission.
Give the next owner a starting point

blocks.title: A brief that can come back with a decision
blocks.caption: Load either example, replace the unresolved assignments and edit the eight sections. The exported sheet records the intended result and its stopping rule; filling it does not certify the plan or authorize work.

blocks.text: The two examples ask for different purchases. One seeks a correction to a recorded device failure. The other buys a small experiment about whether a second day would have a consequential choice. The latter must not arrive disguised as a promise to build the whole game. The preserved Day 2 boundary is a starting constraint, not an implemented future.

The successor’s first hour is a useful measure of the package. There is a specimen to open, an observation to reproduce, obligations to preserve and a decision to bring back. A failed attempt belongs on that path if it changes what the successor should try. A long transcript may remain behind a source link when a short account of the failure does the immediate work. Preserving everything in the same foreground can make the useful beginning disappear.

The stopping line is where the sheet becomes difficult. “Improve until good” lets every discovery enlarge the assignment. “Return one measured repair, or the evidence that the proposed cause was wrong” permits a failed repair to finish a useful piece of work. The owner receives a new fact instead of another obligation disguised as progress. That is a smaller promise, and one whose fulfillment can finally be recognized.

blocks.title: Run one bounded commission
blocks.body: Use the downloadable protocol with the editable sheet. It works for a generated asset, a data pipeline, a game action or a browser feature; the receiving evidence must change with the job.
steps: Choose one recipient and one useful difference. Pin the starting result and the obligations that must survive.
Give the implementer a complete small slice and access to the observation that can reject it. Separate work only where the receiving boundary is explicit.
Inspect the exact returned specimen. Record repair, acceptance, deferral or stop together with the reason and remaining resource allowance.
Hand over the runnable result, evidence and unresolved findings. A successor gets a new commission; a failed check does not silently restart the old one.
blocks.exercise: Take one unfinished item from your own work. Write the smallest investigation that could make you decide against continuing it. If no possible result would change your decision, reconsider what the investigation is for.

blocks.text: At the end of the recorded day, Ed still has Bob’s card. That retained fact made a second encounter tempting before we had settled what the first day was worth. It can remain there now, in a world that opens and runs, with its unfinished work named beside it. The next owner may choose to make Bob ask for it. Nothing in the package should make that choice on their behalf.
